name: Dietary Protein
summary: Dietary protein supplies amino acids for tissue structure, enzymes, transport proteins, immune molecules and oncotic pressure. Severe deficiency produces protein-energy malnutrition.

conditions.label: Deficiency (protein-energy malnutrition)
conditions.description: Inadequate protein (kwashiorkor) or combined protein-energy lack (marasmus) damages multiple systems.

affects.detail: Impaired lipoprotein export causes fat accumulation and an enlarged, soft liver.
Low plasma albumin lowers oncotic pressure, causing pitting oedema and ascites; skin and hair changes ('flag sign') appear in kwashiorkor.

ageModifiers.child: Kwashiorkor typically appears in young children after weaning: oedema, irritability, a distended belly and a reddish tint to the hair.

affects.detail: The body catabolises muscle for amino acids and energy, causing severe wasting and loss of subcutaneous fat.

ageModifiers.infant: Marasmus in infancy produces extreme thinness, an aged ('old man') face and growth failure.
ageModifiers.elderly: Sarcopenia from inadequate protein worsens frailty, falls and recovery from illness.

affects.detail: Reduced synthesis of immune proteins and haemoglobin raises infection risk and contributes to anaemia.
